fields.h1: Build a Needs Assessment Survey That Shows Where to Act First
fields.hero_description: Create a needs assessment survey that shows which needs go unmet for which group, with every answer in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: How the Survey Turns Ratings Into Priorities
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds all six from a plain-English prompt, and you change any of them the same way.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted from your decision

Describe the people you serve and the decision the results will settle. Emergent drafts the list of needs and the wording of each item, and a follow-up prompt rewrites any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Two ratings per need, one gap score

Each need gets two ratings on a scale of 1 to 5: how important it is and how well it is met today. The survey subtracts the second from the first and ranks every need by the gap.
fields.feature_3:
Answers split by group

Every answer lands in a database you own, next to the details you chose to ask for, such as neighborhood, team, or age. Filter the ranking by any of them to see whose needs differ.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts when a gap crosses your line

Set a line, such as a gap of 2.0, and name who acts on it. When a need crosses that line, or a respondent asks to be contacted, that person gets a Slack or email alert.
fields.feature_5:
No cap on answers

Emergent puts no cap on survey responses, so a county with 40,000 households can ask every one of them. Reminders go only to the people on your list who have not answered yet.
fields.feature_6:
Your own domain and a full code export

Publish the survey on your own domain, included with Emergent and paid in credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and run next year's round from it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Surveys and the Top Need Each Found
fields.tab_content_1:
Child care leads with a 2.7-point gap

Harlow County Community Action asks residents to rate 6 services on a 1 to 5 scale, for importance and for how easy each is to get today. Of 612 residents, child care scored 4.6 for importance and 1.9 for access, a gap of 2.7. Housing came next at 2.1. Any gap of 2.0 or more goes into the board's draft plan.
fields.tab_content_2:
Front desk training that starts with insurance checks

Every employee at Brightwater Dental rates 8 skills on how much their job uses each and how confident they feel. Each answer carries a team, pulled from the HR system's API. By the close, 96 of 140 staff had answered. The front desk's widest gap is insurance checks, at 2.2, and the training lead books that course first.
fields.tab_content_3:
Permits slow down 71 of the businesses that answered

Millbrook's economic development office emails a short survey to 300 local businesses. Each picks the barrier that holds it back most and can ask for a call. Of the 184 that answered, 71 picked permits. Fenwick Print Shop wrote that a sign permit took 9 weeks. Its answer went straight to the business liaison.
fields.tab_content_4:
Getting to appointments comes first in Eastgate

Northgate Regional Hospital posts QR codes in clinic waiting rooms, and patients answer on their phones after picking a neighborhood. In Eastgate, 90 of 220 answers named getting to appointments as the biggest barrier, against 98 of 815 elsewhere. The hospital's plan adds a weekday shuttle from Eastgate.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Needs Assessment Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a needs assessment survey whose gap scores tell you what to fix first.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Start from the data you already hold
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 List the needs in plain words
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the choice the results feed, such as which 2 services get next year's grant money or which course runs first. Every item on the survey should inform that choice. Put the decision at the top of your prompt, and Emergent drafts the needs around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pull what intake records, census tables, or last year's round already tell you, and drop the questions they answer. Ask people only what no record holds, such as why they stopped using a service or what they would use if it existed.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Keep the list between 6 and 12 needs, each named the way your group would say it: help paying rent, not housing cost burden. Split any item that bundles two needs, since a double-barreled item asks people to judge more than one thing at once.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask how important each need is, then how well current services cover it, using one scale for both. The difference is the gap. A need rated 5 and met at 4 matters less to your plan than one rated 4 and met at 1.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add the 2 or 3 details you will split results by, such as neighborhood or household size, and make them optional where you can. A gap that looks small county-wide can be the top need in one neighborhood.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it before it goes out
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit 5 test answers with ratings you chose and check that each gap comes out right and that alerts reach their owner. Then have a few people from the group take it: Pew Research Center calls pretesting an essential step for seeing how people respond.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Rank the gaps and report back
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sort the needs by gap, then compare the top few across groups before you decide. Tell the people who answered which need you will act on first and when, using the same channel that reached them for the survey.

faq_plan.q: What is a needs assessment survey?
faq_plan.ref: What is a needs assessment survey?

prov.original: What is a needs assessment survey?

faq_plan.a: A needs assessment survey asks a defined group, such as residents or staff, what they need and how well those needs are met today. The gap between the two shows where money and staff time will do the most good.

faq_plan.q: How do you create a needs assessment survey?
faq_plan.ref: how to create a needs assessment survey
faq_plan.a: Describe the group, the needs you want rated, and the decision the results feed. Emergent's AI survey builder drafts the paired ratings and the table that stores every answer. Publish it as a link or a QR code, then change any item with a follow-up prompt.

faq_plan.q: What are some good survey questions for a needs assessment?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good survey questions for a needs assessment?

prov.original: What are some good survey questions for a needs assessment?

faq_plan.a: Good needs assessment survey questions ask about one need at a time and pair two ratings. How important is reliable child care to your household, 1 to 5? How easy is it to find today? Add an open question on what stopped someone from using a service in the past year, and one on which single change would help most.

faq_plan.q: Do you need to validate a needs assessment survey?
faq_plan.ref: do you need to validate a needs assessment survey
faq_plan.a: Not formally, unless you will publish the results or compare scores with other studies. For an internal survey, a quick check is enough: ask 3 people from the group to say in their own words what each question means, and rewrite any item they read differently. An exit survey that only guides your own decisions gets the same light check.

faq_plan.q: What is a community needs assessment survey?
faq_plan.ref: what is a community needs assessment survey
faq_plan.a: A community needs assessment survey asks the people in a county or service area which local needs go unmet, such as housing or child care. Charitable hospitals must conduct a community health needs assessment every three years, according to the IRS. It has to take into account input from people who represent the broad interests of the community the hospital serves.

faq_plan.q: What is the purpose of a needs assessment survey?
faq_plan.ref: what is the purpose of a needs assessment survey
faq_plan.a: The purpose of a needs assessment survey is to decide where limited money and staff time go, based on what people report rather than what an organization assumes. It also gives a funder or board a documented reason for each choice. A survey built with Emergent keeps the answers in your own database, ready to compare item by item with next year's round.

faq_plan.q: Is a needs assessment survey template worth using?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as a checklist, not as the finished survey. A needs assessment survey template lists someone else's needs: cut every item no decision depends on, and add the ones your group would name. Skip templates made for other jobs; a brand perception survey asks how people see you, not what they lack. Emergent drafts a first version from a description of your group.

faq_plan.q: What should a training needs survey ask?
faq_plan.a: A training needs survey should list the skills each role uses and ask two things about each: how much the job relies on it and how confident the person feels doing it. Ask managers to rate their team on the same skills and compare the two views. Add one question on preferred format, such as short sessions or a full-day course.

faq_plan.q: How do you conduct a needs assessment survey?
faq_plan.ref: how to conduct a needs assessment survey
faq_plan.a: Decide first whether to ask everyone or a sample, and set a target number of answers for each group you plan to compare. Offer more than one way in, such as an emailed link and a QR code at the front desk. Watch the count per group while the survey runs, push harder where one lags, and close on a set date so every group gets the same window.

faq_plan.q: How do you develop a needs assessment survey?
faq_plan.ref: how to develop a needs assessment survey
faq_plan.a: Start by listening: talk to 6 to 8 people from the group and note the needs they name, in their words. Turn each into one item and have the people who will act on the results review the list. Ask once whether people know each service exists, since nobody uses a program they have not heard of. Stop there, or it becomes a brand awareness survey.

plan.angle: The top 10 is guides and sample PDFs (Community Tool Box, CDC, Indeed, state agencies, a preservation leaflet) plus one Microsoft Forms survey and one software vendor's template post. They explain what a needs assessment is but leave the hard part, turning answers into a ranked list of gaps, to a spreadsheet. This page answers the informational intent in the FAQ (definition, good questions, validation, community and training versions, purpose, how to conduct and develop one) and then shows four needs assessment surveys built from a prompt that rate each need twice and rank the gap: residents for a community action agency, dental staff for training, local businesses for a city, and a hospital's service area by neighborhood. The community survey sibling owns town votes and pantry polls; this page owns gap ranking.

Millbrook's economic development office asks 300 local businesses for their biggest barrier, 71 of the 184 that answer pick permits, and Fenwick Print Shop's comment that a sign permit took 9 weeks goes to the business liaison because it ticked contact me.
